settings.name: ELTRIX_DOMAIN
settings.purpose: The Matrix `server_name`. Appears in every user ID and every event signature, so it is permanent by construction: events signed under one name can never be re-signed under another. Different from PHX_HOST.

settings.name: PHX_HOST
settings.purpose: The hostname the listener answers on. An address, not an identity — it never reaches a user ID. On www it differs from ELTRIX_DOMAIN because the apex delegates; on beta the two are equal because it does not.

settings.name: PHX_SERVER
settings.purpose: Set to start the web listener. A release without it boots and serves nothing.

settings.name: PORT
settings.purpose: The one listener for client, federation and key APIs. TLS terminates at the edge, so this is plain HTTP.

settings.name: METRICS_PORT
settings.purpose: A separate listener for Prometheus metrics, so they are never publicly routed by sharing a port with the API.

settings.name: SECRET_KEY_BASE
settings.purpose: Signs and encrypts session cookies and tokens.

settings.name: DATABASE_URL
settings.purpose: The Postgres connection URL. Note the pooler: production points at postgres-pooler-rw, which is shared with every other product on the cluster, so a transaction held open elsewhere is visible to us.

settings.name: POOL_SIZE
settings.purpose: Database connections held open per node. Sync is a long poll, so this bounds concurrent syncs as much as it bounds queries.

settings.name: ECTO_IPV6
settings.purpose: Connect to Postgres over IPv6. Needed where the cluster has no IPv4 path.

settings.name: CLUSTER_DNS_QUERY
settings.purpose: Headless Service DNS name whose A records are the other pods, for BEAM clustering. Unset means no topology at all, so the node never looks for peers — the correct default while replicas are 1.

settings.name: CLUSTER_NODE_BASENAME
settings.purpose: The part before the @ in each node name. It has to match what the release sets as RELEASE_NODE, or the strategy builds names nothing answers to and reports no error at all.

settings.name: REGISTRATION_ENABLED
settings.purpose: Set to `false` to refuse every registration, invitation or not.

settings.default: true in prod, false in dev and test
settings.name: REGISTRATION_REQUIRES_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Registration needs an invitation from /admin/invites. Defaults to `true` in prod: a deployment that sets nothing must not be an open server. It defaulted to `false` once, and a publicly reachable homeserver was open for six minutes.

settings.name: FEDERATION_ENABLED
settings.purpose: Whether the federation API exists at all. Off means every federation endpoint answers 404 M_UNRECOGNIZED, which is how a peer feature-detects a server that does not federate. Separate from an empty allowlist.

settings.name: FEDERATION_ALLOWLIST
settings.purpose: Comma-separated server names that may send to us or be dialled by us (D3). Unset refuses everyone — the opposite default would turn a missing variable into open federation. Exactly `*` federates with the whole network, which is a deliberate act and is logged as a warning at boot.

settings.default: empty, which dials only public addresses
settings.name: FEDERATION_IP_ALLOWLIST
settings.purpose: Comma-separated CIDRs a federation request may be dialled into despite not being routable on the public internet. Empty by default, which is the SSRF guard doing its job; needed when a peer is on the same private network, and by the conformance harness.

settings.default: the compiled default, which is `info` in production
settings.name: LOG_LEVEL
settings.purpose: The minimum level written to the log. `info` is what makes the federation refusal line visible — a refused peer is an ordinary event on a public endpoint rather than a fault, so it is not a warning.

settings.name: MEDIA_S3_ENDPOINT
settings.purpose: The S3-compatible object store media lives in. Required in prod: a deployment with nowhere to put media is misconfigured whether or not anybody has uploaded anything, and it used to fail as a 500 on the first upload instead of at boot.

settings.name: MEDIA_S3_BUCKET
settings.purpose: Bucket the media objects live in. SigV4 signs it, so it cannot be changed by rewriting a URL, and the gateway allowlists it separately.

settings.name: MEDIA_S3_REGION
settings.purpose: SigV4 region. Garage does not use it for placement but signs it.

settings.name: MEDIA_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
settings.purpose: Object storage key, scoped to the one bucket with owner false, so the application cannot change bucket settings even if the key leaks.

settings.name: MEDIA_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
settings.purpose: Secret half of the object storage key pair. Never logged and never rendered into the generated configuration table.

settings.name: ELTRIX_TLS_CERTFILE
settings.purpose: Certificate for a second listener that speaks TLS. Production terminates TLS at the edge and sets none of these; the conformance harness sets them because it expects federation on its own certificate.

settings.name: ELTRIX_TLS_KEYFILE
settings.purpose: Private key for that certificate. Required whenever the certificate is set.

settings.name: ELTRIX_TLS_PORT
settings.purpose: Port for the TLS listener. 8448 is the Matrix federation default, which is what the conformance harness expects.

settings.name: RATE_LIMIT_ALLOWANCE
settings.purpose: Multiplies every rate-limit window. 1 in production, 40 in dev where there are no strangers, and higher in the conformance harness, which registers dozens of accounts in seconds and would otherwise fail tests on a 429 during their setup.

settings.name: APPSERVICE_REGISTRATIONS
settings.purpose: Colon-separated paths to application-service registration files (§4.2.6). Read once at boot and never written by the server: a bridge that could register itself could grant itself a namespace, and the namespace is the authorisation. Unset means no services, which is inert; a file that is present and unparseable is fatal, because a bridge with silently no namespace fails in a way neither end can see.

settings.name: SMTP_RELAY
settings.purpose: SMTP relay for 3PID verification and password-reset mail (§4.2.1). Postal, not Postmark, and that is a domain fact rather than a preference: the eltrix.org zone allows only Stalwart and Postal to send as it, with DMARC p=reject, so Postmark mail fails DMARC at every recipient and arrives nowhere. Unset means 3PID cannot send; everything else still works.

settings.name: SMTP_PORT
settings.purpose: Where the relay listens. 25 in-cluster rather than 587, because this is a submission to our own Postal over the pod network and not a hop across the internet; TLS is still required on it (see SMTP_TLS_SERVER_NAME).

settings.name: SMTP_USERNAME
settings.purpose: The Postal credential, written `organisation/server` — it names a mail server inside Postal rather than a person, and which one decides which domains the mail may claim to be from.

settings.name: SMTP_PASSWORD
settings.purpose: The key belonging to that credential. Rotating it in Postal without updating this stops 3PID mail and nothing else, so the symptom is a verification code that never arrives.

settings.name: SMTP_TLS_SERVER_NAME
settings.purpose: The hostname the relay's certificate is issued for. Named explicitly because the relay is reached at its in-cluster Service name while its certificate is for smtp.postal.oddie.app; without it verification fails on a name mismatch and every send is refused by our own side, which looks exactly like a credential problem.

settings.name: MAIL_FROM
settings.purpose: The address verification mail is sent from. The app's own domain, never a shared one — a code that arrives from somewhere unrelated to the server reads as phishing, which is exactly what it would be teaching people to accept.

settings.name: MAIL_FROM_NAME
settings.purpose: The display name on verification mail.

settings.name: MEDIA_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES
settings.purpose: Largest upload accepted, advertised to clients through /_matrix/media/v3/config, so raising it is all a client needs.
